title: Nineteen Years and One Empty Site
subtitle: 发展与进步 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 发展与进步（科学与技术·发展与进步）
meta: 主题语境：发展与进步（科学与技术·发展与进步）　|　核心词汇：development　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 development 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1952 the planner ① approved a development that no council in the district would have funded, and he said the approving was the whole of the scheme. The ② development, meaning the building work and not the progress, ran nineteen years and stayed unfinished on the site; a development, he said, is the only thing in a scheme that is judged by how long it is left unbuilt.

Every ③ development in that district had the same empty site at the middle of it, and the ④ development at the end, meaning the one they kept for the housing and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever inspected twice. A development, his assistant said, is nine parts paperwork and one part somebody willing to approve; the planner said the paperwork is the part that fills nineteen years.

The economist meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the development was the whole of the region, meaning the progress and not the building work. The ⑥ development, meaning the progress and not any of that, is the only thing in a region that everybody measures and nobody doubts; development, she said, is either something you approve or the only word that means both building work and progress. She said the progress is the part they remember.

By 1963 the ⑦ development had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the empty site. The ⑧ development of the whole thing, the planner wrote in November, was one district and nineteen years of paperwork; development, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to approve. She said the approving was never mentioned.

The ⑨ development I remember is the one at the end, which was finished in 1978 and is still described as the slowest in the district. A ⑩ development, the assistant said in 1980, is the only thing that improves by being finished; every development, she said, is a progress that has agreed to look like building work. She said the progress was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 开发项目；建设（指那个区里获批的那一项）
B. n. 开发（指那些建设工程本身，与那种进步相对）
C. 固定搭配：approve a development 批准一项开发
D. n. 开发项目（指留给住宅用的那一项）
E. n. 开发；建设（抽象总称，指一个区里的全部开发）
F. n. 开发项目（指规划图上写到、被列明的那一项）
G. n. 发展；进步（指一个地区的发展水平）
H. n. 发展（抽象总称，指人人衡量却无人怀疑的那种）

items.q: approved a development that no council in the district would have funded
The development, meaning the building work and not the progress
the development was the whole of the region
the development had become a line in a plan
The development of the whole thing
A development, the assistant said in 1980

answers.why: approve a development 意为“批准一项开发”，1952 年规划员批准了一项全区没有一处议会肯出资的开发。
development 意为“开发”，指那些建设工程本身而不是那种进步，它在工地上历经十九年而没有完工。
development 意为“开发项目”，指那个区里每一项开发，每一项中间都有同一块空地。
development 意为“开发项目”，指留给住宅用的那一项，是唯一有人视察过两次的。
development 意为“发展、进步”，指一个地区的发展水平，经济学家说这种发展就是那个地区的全部。
development 意为“发展”，指人人衡量却无人怀疑的那种而不是那些建设工程，是地区里人人都衡量、却无人怀疑的东西。
development 意为“开发项目”，指规划图上写到、被列明的那一项，到 1963 年这项开发成了规划图上的一行。
development 意为“开发、建设”，规划员十一月写道，整件事的建设是一个区和十九年的文书。
development 意为“开发项目”，我记得的是末尾那一项，1978 年完工，至今仍被说成全区最慢的一项。
development 为抽象总称，助手 1980 年说，一项开发是唯一会因为被建成而变得更好的东西。
